findings.title: 22 'Title overline too short' warnings: zero-warning 1.0 bar failed by example docstring title markup
findings.description: The build emits exactly 24 warnings; 22 are 'Title overline too short.' at line 21 of generated gallery pages. Root cause is in the SOURCE examples: docstring titles use '=' over/underlines shorter than the title text (e.g. examples/plot_sotus.py: 29 '=' chars over the 56-char title 'Plotting State of the Union Addresses with Text Analysis'). Affected (from build1.log): animate_MDS, animate_plotly, animate_trails_mix, plot_PPCA, plot_TSNE, plot_UMAP, plot_align, plot_apply_model, plot_clusters2, plot_clusters3, plot_corpus, plot_describe, plot_digits, plot_geo, plot_impute, plot_interactive_backend, plot_missing_data, plot_mixture_models, plot_nested_lists, plot_predict, plot_procrustes, plot_sotus. Titles still render (docutils recovers) so impact is warning noise only, but the stated 1.0 bar is zero warnings. Fix: lengthen the '=' lines to >= title length in those 22 example files.

findings.title: Sphinx cannot cache the build environment: unpickleable sphinx_gallery_conf warning on every build
findings.description: conf.py puts a function reference (plotly_sg_scraper fallback def) and computed first_notebook_cell into sphinx_gallery_conf, so Sphinx 9 warns it cannot pickle the config into the environment cache on every build. Harmless for this Makefile (html target passes -E anyway) but is 1/24 warnings against the zero-warning bar. Fix options: add suppress_warnings = ['config.cache'] to conf.py (the sphinx-gallery-documented remedy) or reference the scraper by string name.

findings.title: 9 shipped gallery pages contain baked-in warning blocks leaking machine-local paths (/Users/jmanning/...)
findings.description: The cached (committed) sphinx-gallery outputs embed runtime warnings, each prefixed with an absolute path from the build machine, visible to every docs reader: animate_MDS (2x sklearn FutureWarning: MDS n_init/init defaults will change), plot_clusters3 (HDBSCAN FutureWarning), plot_PPCA + plot_missing_data (hypertools UserWarning 'Missing data: Inexact solution computed with PPCA' AND hypertools' own matplotlib_backend.py:102 UserWarning 'linestyle is redundantly defined...'), plot_text + plot_sotus (sklearn InconsistentVersionWarning unpickling the hosted model), plot_describe (UserWarning 'this computation can take a long time'), plot_hue (numpy DeprecationWarning raised BY THE EXAMPLE CODE, examples/plot_hue.py:31 'Conversion of an array with ndim > 0 to a scalar is deprecated' -- will hard-error on future numpy), plot_impute. Beyond polish, the FutureWarning/DeprecationWarning items flag examples that will change or break under upcoming sklearn/numpy. Fix: silence-or-fix warnings in the examples (preferred: fix the code paths) and re-render; consider a warnings filter in the gallery config only where the warning is intentional teaching content.
findings.expected: no machine-local paths or unexplained warning blocks in published example output
findings.actual: 9 files match: animate_MDS.rst plot_PPCA.rst plot_clusters3.rst plot_describe.rst plot_hue.rst plot_sotus.rst plot_impute.rst plot_missing_data.rst plot_text.rst; e.g. plot_hue.rst:47 '/Users/jmanning/hypertools/examples/plot_hue.py:31: DeprecationWarning: Conversion of an array with ndim > 0 to a scalar is deprecated'

findings.title: Docs build executes plot_datasets_tour against the live network (fivethirtyeight CSV + kaggle download) when stale
findings.description: plot_datasets_tour.py was md5-stale and re-executed during this build, fetching remote data at build time: its fresh output shows 'fivethirtyeight: bechdel: (1794, 15)' and 'kaggle: uciml/iris: (150, 6)'. findings.title: make html on any branch rewrites tracked docs/auto_examples artifacts and bakes the branch name into all downloadable notebooks
findings.description: The gallery outputs (.rst/.ipynb/.md5/.zip/images) are committed, and conf.py's _install_notebook_cell() embeds the CURRENT git branch into the first cell of every generated notebook (all 53, plus both download zips). This build (on audit/release-1.0-2026-07) modified 24 tracked files and produced notebooks whose install cell is '%pip install -q "hypertools[interactive] @ git+https://github.com/ContextLab/hypertools.git@audit/release-1.0-2026-07"' -- an ephemeral branch URL that will dangle after the branch is deleted. Any contributor building docs on a feature branch dirties the tree the same way (the fix/qc-notes branch snapshot showed identical churn). For release this must be built from master (cell then becomes '%pip install -q "hypertools[interactive]"'). Consider excluding branch-derived content from committed artifacts or generating install cells at publish time only.

findings.expected: docs build leaves the tree clean; published notebooks reference a stable install target

findings.title: Story-trajectories docstring: runtime claim off by ~20x and its recommended kernel_width triggers a UserWarning
findings.description: examples/plot_story_trajectories.py says 'The full pipeline takes a couple of minutes on the full dataset, so this example does not re-run it live'. Verbatim execution of the exact documented code block (36 subjects, full manip+hyperalign+animated mp4 export) completed in 6.9 s on this machine -- the stated justification overstates cost ~20x. The same documented spec uses kernel_width=40 (even), which emits 'UserWarning: Increasing smoothing kernel width by 1 (must be odd)' -- the docs' own recommended parameters warn. Numeric claims in the same prose DO reproduce (dispersion 0.643 vs '~0.64' for the reduce-to-10d-then-align baseline; 0.466 vs '~0.47' aligned-then-reduced; drop 27.5% vs tutorials.rst '~30%'). Suggest: kernel_width=41, and either run the example live or soften the runtime claim.
findings.expected: documented snippet runs warning-free; prose runtime matches reality
findings.actual: hypertools/manip/smooth.py:172: UserWarning: Increasing smoothing kernel width by 1 (must be odd) | VERBATIM SNIPPET OK in 6.9s; mp4 size: 2284872 | scale=rms_global: wrong=0.750 right=0.466; 10d-baseline=0.643

findings.title: Furo edit/view-source links target master; Makefile invokes bare `python` for post_build
findings.description: (a) html_theme_options source_branch = 'master': the per-page GitHub source links 404 for any page whose source is not yet on master (all dev-1.0 content until merge). Harmless at release-from-master, wrong for previews. (b) docs/Makefile html target runs 'python post_build.py' with bare `python`; on macOS/CI environments without a `python` shim (only python3), make html dies AFTER a successful sphinx-build, at the thumbnail-fix step. This audit's build succeeded only because the venv bin (which has `python`) was prepended to PATH.
findings.expected: branch-aware source links (like the notebook cell already is); python3/$(PYTHON) in Makefile
